user.title: Connect to the pfSense firewall / router
user.description: Choose the API Home Assistant should use. **Netgate API** is pfSense's built-in API (the Nexus controller, standard from 26.10). The other options use the community REST API package, which stops working when Netgate removes PHP from pfSense.

menu_options.basic: REST API package — username and password
menu_options.jwt: REST API package — JWT (from username and password)

netgate.title: Netgate API (Nexus)
netgate.description:
Enter the firewall's Netgate API address, including the port (usually 8443, e.g. {example_url}), and a pfSense user's credentials. The user must be in the `admins` group or in the Nexus `mim_…` groups for the features you use.

The API port is **not** covered by pfSense's anti-lockout rule: if Home Assistant cannot connect, add a LAN pass rule from the Home Assistant host to that port.

api_key.title: pfSense REST API — API key
api_key.description: Enter the base URL of the pfSense REST API (including the port, e.g. {example_url}) and an API key generated at System › REST API › Keys.

basic.title: pfSense REST API — username and password
basic.description: Enter the base URL of the pfSense REST API (including the port, e.g. {example_url}) and a pfSense local user's credentials. HTTP Basic authentication must be enabled at System › REST API › Settings.

jwt.title: pfSense REST API — JWT
jwt.description: Enter the base URL of the pfSense REST API (including the port, e.g. {example_url}) and a pfSense local user's credentials. Home Assistant obtains and refreshes a JWT from them. JWT authentication must be enabled at System › REST API › Settings.

reconfigure.title: Change how Home Assistant connects
reconfigure.description: Choose the API to use from now on. The firewall must stay the same: entities, history and automations are kept. To move off the community REST API package, choose **Netgate API**.

menu_options.reconfigure_basic: REST API package — username and password
menu_options.reconfigure_jwt: REST API package — JWT (from username and password)

error.invalid_auth: Authentication failed — check the credentials. For the REST API package, also check that this method is enabled at System › REST API › Settings.
error.privilege_missing: The account lacks the privileges this integration needs (REST API package: the api-v2 privileges; Netgate API: the admins group or the mim_… groups).
error.api_not_found: No pfSense API at that URL — check the address and port, and that the API is enabled (Netgate API: usually port 8443; REST API package: install and enable it).

abort.wrong_device: That URL and those credentials reach a different pfSense device. Reconfigure must keep the same firewall; add a new entry for a different one.

data.rule_switch_kill_states: Reset matching states when a rule switch is toggled
data.firmware_install_unverified: Allow firmware install from Home Assistant (experimental, not yet verified)

data_description.firmware_install_unverified: Adds an Install button to the firmware update entity (Netgate API only). The upgrade call is built from Netgate's API documentation and has not been tested on a real upgrade yet. The firewall reboots while upgrading. Leave this off unless you are ready to recover from the console if it goes wrong.

device_tracker.description: Choose which devices you want to track.

cannot_connect.title: {name}: pfSense is not reachable
cannot_connect.description:
Home Assistant has not reached the pfSense API at {url} for several polls. Last error: `{error}`.

Entities show cached data for a few minutes, then become unavailable.

To fix:
1. Check the firewall is up and that {url} opens from the Home Assistant host.
2. **Check a firewall rule lets the Home Assistant host reach port {port} on the firewall.** pfSense's anti-lockout rule only covers the web GUI port; the Netgate Nexus API (usually 8443) needs its own LAN rule (Pass, TCP, source = the HA host, destination = LAN address, port {port}).
3. If the address or port changed, delete and re-add the integration with the new URL.

This notice clears itself once a poll succeeds.

tls_error.title: {name}: TLS certificate not trusted
tls_error.description:
The pfSense API at {url} answered, but its TLS certificate could not be verified. Last error: `{error}`.

To fix, either:
- give the firewall's API a certificate Home Assistant trusts (e.g. from the ACME package), or
- if the firewall uses its default self-signed certificate, re-add the integration with **Verify SSL certificate** turned off.

This notice clears itself once a poll succeeds.

api_missing.title: {name}: pfSense API not found
api_missing.description:
{url} answered but has no pfSense API at that address (HTTP 404). Last error: `{error}`.

To fix:
- **REST API package:** install it under System › Package Manager and enable it under System › REST API, and make sure the URL includes the port the API listens on (often the web GUI port).
- **Netgate Nexus API:** enable it under System › Advanced › Netgate Nexus and use the HTTPS port shown there.

This notice clears itself once a poll succeeds.

api_error.title: {name}: pfSense API is returning errors
api_error.description:
The pfSense API at {url} is reachable but keeps failing. Last error: `{error}`.

Check the firewall's system log and the API package's status. If the problem started after a pfSense or package update, report it with the integration's diagnostics download (Settings › Devices & services › pfSense › ⋮ › Download diagnostics).

This notice clears itself once a poll succeeds.

privilege_missing.title: {name}: missing API privileges
privilege_missing.description:
The account Home Assistant uses is not allowed to read: **{checks}**. Those parts of the integration show stale or no data; everything else keeps working.

To fix, in System › User Manager on the firewall:
- **REST API package:** give the user the matching `api-v2-…-get` privileges (or `WebCfg - All pages`), plus the write privileges for anything you control from Home Assistant.
- **Netgate Nexus API:** add the user to a Nexus group such as `mim_read_system`, `mim_read_firewall`, `mim_read_interfaces` or `mim_read_services` (or `mim_modify_…` for control).

This notice clears itself once those checks succeed.

pfrest_eol.title: {name}: the REST API package is end-of-life
pfrest_eol.description:
This connection uses the community REST API package, which stops working once Netgate removes PHP from pfSense. This firewall is already running Netgate's built-in API (the Nexus controller), which is the supported replacement.

Nothing is broken yet. To switch, open this integration's entry, choose **Reconfigure**, then **Netgate API**. Your entities are kept. Details: {migration_url}

certificate_expiring.title: {name}: certificate expiring
certificate_expiring.description:
These certificates on the firewall expire soon or have expired: **{certificates}**.

Renew or replace them in System › Certificates, or in Services › ACME for ACME certificates. This notice clears itself once no tracked certificate is within 14 days of expiry.
